topic: What a block header holds: the previous hash and the merkle root
hook: Bitcoin miners don't hash the whole block. Just 80 bytes.

scenes.narration: Here is the surprise. Miners only run proof of work on the 80-byte block header.
That header holds the previous block's hash, which links the chain together, plus the merkle root of the block's transactions.
It also has a nonce, an easy field to change, so miners can try fresh hashes over and over.
Every attempt changes only that tiny nonce, and the header is hashed again.

cta: Which part surprised you most? Tell me below, and the link is on my channel page.
title: Bitcoin Miners Only Hash 80 Bytes
description_body: Only the 80-byte block header is hashed for proof of work. It stores the previous block hash, the merkle root and a nonce.
